params.name: p.motion_speed_floor
params.convention: motion-resolution convention: below this speed a sampled velocity carries no reliable direction, so the road user counts as not travelling
params.source: trajectory-processing practice for naturalistic driving data (velocity noise floor of GNSS/INS tracks)

params.name: p.direction_opposition_cosine
params.convention: heading-opposition tolerance, as the oncoming relation states it: the cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed that still counts as opposed (here sixty degrees)
params.source: conflict-analysis practice for opposed-direction encounters

params.name: p.standstill_speed_tolerance
params.convention: standstill-detection convention: the speed at or below which a sampled track counts as showing no movement, set at the noise floor of the speed measurement so that a complete cessation is recognized without being asserted of a creeping vehicle
params.source: instrumented-vehicle and trajectory-processing practice for stop-sign compliance studies

params.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
params.convention: stop-bar compliance convention: the distance behind the marked line within which a halt counts as made at the line
params.source: traffic-engineering practice for stop-line compliance measurement

params.name: p.cautious_speed_max
params.convention: low-speed re-entry convention: the entry speed from a required halt at which a driver retains the ability to abort within the junction, taken as the ten-mile-per-hour crawl speed used for failed-signal and all-way-stop operation
params.source: traffic-engineering guidance on operation at dark or failed signals

params.name: p.conflict_horizon
params.convention: gap-acceptance convention: the look-ahead over which a constant-velocity projection is taken to represent an imminent conflict at junction speeds
params.source: surrogate safety measure practice (time-to-conflict horizons in conflict analysis)

params.name: p.conflict_clearance
params.convention: gap-acceptance convention: the centre-to-centre clearance at closest approach below which the projected passage is taken to disturb the other road user
params.source: surrogate safety measure practice (post-encroachment and minimum-separation thresholds)

params.name: p.view_sight_distance_min
params.convention: intersection sight-distance convention: the distance along the through way within which an approaching vehicle must be visible from a position for that position to count as one from which the driver has a view of approaching traffic, taken from the departure sight triangle for a through way of ordinary urban through speed
params.source: AASHTO Green Book, intersection sight distance (departure sight triangles, Case B); MUTCD practice on stop-line and stop-sign placement

params.name: p.reasonable_speed_base
params.convention: basic-speed-rule convention: the speed a dry, clear, straight way of full lane width, free of other traffic and with long sight distance, supports as reasonable and proper, taken as the design speed of an ordinary undivided rural highway
params.source: AASHTO Green Book design speeds for rural arterials; enforcement practice under state basic-speed rules

params.name: p.lane_width_reference
params.convention: lane-width convention: the design lane width against which the width available to the vehicle is scaled, so that a narrower lane lowers the bound in proportion to its width
params.source: AASHTO Green Book design lane widths

params.name: p.lateral_accel_max
params.convention: curve-speed convention: the lateral acceleration a driver of ordinary skill accepts on a horizontal curve, which with the roadway's curvature bounds the speed - the square of the speed does not exceed this acceleration divided by the curvature
params.source: AASHTO Green Book side-friction factors for horizontal curves

params.name: p.sight_time
params.convention: assured-clear-distance convention: the time within which the vehicle must be able to be brought to rest within the distance that can be seen ahead, so the bound is the sighted distance divided by this time; it folds the perception-reaction time and the braking time of the stopping-sight-distance model into one constant
params.source: AASHTO Green Book stopping sight distance (perception-reaction plus braking distance)

params.name: p.traffic_headway_time
params.convention: headway convention: the time gap to the nearest road user ahead in the same lane that the speed must leave, so the bound is the longitudinal surface gap divided by this time
params.source: car-following headway guidance (AASHTO following-distance practice and the following-distance rule used in driver training)

params.name: p.wet_speed_factor
params.convention: surface-condition convention: the fraction of the dry-road bound that a wet surface leaves, from the reduction of available friction on wet pavement
params.source: AASHTO Green Book wet-pavement friction factors

params.name: p.ice_speed_factor
params.convention: surface-condition convention: the fraction of the dry-road bound that an icy or snow-covered surface leaves, from the reduction of available friction on ice and packed snow
params.source: winter-maintenance pavement-friction measurements; AASHTO friction guidance for winter surfaces

params.name: p.precipitation_speed_factor
params.convention: weather convention: the fraction of the bound that falling rain or snow leaves, from the loss of contrast and of sight distance while precipitation falls
params.source: FHWA Road Weather Management speed-reduction studies

params.name: p.darkness_speed_factor
params.convention: night-driving convention: the fraction of the bound that insufficient natural light leaves, from the shorter distance at which a driver can resolve an object under headlamps
params.source: FHWA and AASHTO guidance on night-time sight distance and headlamp illumination

params.name: p.grade_speed_sensitivity
params.convention: grade convention: the fractional reduction of the bound per unit of downgrade, from the lengthening of braking distance on a descending grade
params.source: AASHTO Green Book grade corrections to stopping sight distance

params.name: p.turn_window
params.convention: manoeuvre-recognition convention: the time behind the observation over which a change of direction is accumulated for it to count as one turn, taken from the duration of a turn through a square junction at junction approach speeds
params.source: turning-path and intersection-design practice (AASHTO Green Book turning paths at 15-25 km/h design speeds)

params.name: p.turn_heading_change
params.convention: manoeuvre-recognition convention: the accumulated heading change that tells a turn from lane-keeping and from a lane change, taken as half of the ninety-degree change of a square junction turn
params.source: manoeuvre-classification practice in naturalistic driving studies (lane-change heading changes below, junction turns above)

params.name: p.yaw_rate_floor
params.convention: motion-resolution convention: below this rate of change of heading a sampled heading carries no reliable rotation, so the road user counts as not turning at that observation
params.source: yaw-rate sensor noise floor used for manoeuvre detection in vehicle dynamics instrumentation

params.name: p.approach_path_window
params.convention: turn-approach convention: the distance travelled before a turn over which the positioning for that turn is judged, taken from the length of the deceleration and storage taper a turning lane provides at an urban junction, within which a vehicle intending to turn is expected to have taken its lane
params.source: turning-lane design practice (AASHTO Green Book deceleration and storage lengths for urban turn bays at 40-50 km/h)

params.name: p.approach_reach
params.convention: intersection approach-zone convention: the distance from a junction within which a vehicle closing on it is near enough that its passage bears on a manoeuvre made in the junction, taken from the leg of the departure sight triangle for a through way of ordinary urban through speed
params.source: intersection sight-distance tables (AASHTO Green Book departure sight triangles, 40-50 km/h approach speeds)

params.name: p.yield_body_clearance
params.convention: gap-acceptance convention: the clearance between the bodies of two vehicles within which the one is taken to intrude on the passage of a vehicle it owes precedence to, measured between the bodies and not between their centres; taken from the one-metre lateral clearance a driver is expected to leave when passing a stationary vehicle at crawl speed, widened for the privileged vehicle's own movement
params.source: lateral-clearance practice for passing a stopped vehicle at crawl speed (one metre), widened by half for the movement of the vehicle with precedence

_fields.params: name (p.<name>), value (number), unit (m|s|m/s|m/s2|deg|deg/s|ratio|count), convention (text), figure_review (optional: why a value that equals a figure some law states is a convention, not that figure)
_fields.aggregates: word (a legal aggregate such as 'vehicle'), classes (ru.* ids it covers)

declarations.meaning: the way the road user is travelling on lies outside the territorial limits of a city, so that it is a road within the meaning of NRS 484A.215 rather than a street; declared per map or per trace, since a city or town limit is a legal region class and nothing on the road displays it

the source's current plan for the road user includes turning, to either side, at the target region: true where that plan holds at the target, false where the plan decides on another manoeuvre, on passing through, or on a turn cancelled or already completed there, and absent where the source has no plan for that road user at that region

the source's current plan for the road user includes turning to the left at the target region: true where that plan holds at the target, false where the plan decides on another manoeuvre, on passing through, or on a turn cancelled or already completed there, and absent where the source has no plan for that road user at that region
